explainedBy: A manager praises while walking off, eyes on the phone, so the praise is dismissed as a passing remark.

storyboard.claim: Drive-by praise is delivered on the way out, not given.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager walks down the hallway looking at a phone in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First beat of the passage; establishes the careless manager.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the manager's attention is elsewhere.

explainedBy: The compliment sandwich: praise, then criticism, then praise; the criticism sits in the middle as the filling.

storyboard.claim: The compliment sandwich puts the criticism in the middle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three buckets: praise, criticism, praise.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the person with the structure of the feedback.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the sandwich order visible.

explainedBy: The brain drops the praise and keeps the criticism; the same sandwich shows which part survives.

storyboard.claim: The brain keeps the criticism and dilutes the praise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same three buckets; the callout marks the criticism as what remains.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same diagram kept; only the callout changes to name what sticks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the outcome of the sandwich.

explainedBy: The manager stops talking and lets the silence hang so Paul can take in the praise.

storyboard.claim: The good manager holds a pause after praise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager stands still beside Paul, quiet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Diagram gives way to the two people in the office.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pause as a deliberate act.

explainedBy: Feedback is worth most when it comes close to the moment, so timing is the point.
noVisual: No food icon: a food icon reads as literal dining, not as timing.

storyboard.claim: Feedback has to arrive while it still matters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager speaks to the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager alone again; the pause is over.
storyboard.addedInformation: Text carries the metaphor.

explainedBy: Praise given months late loses its emotional effect; the clock shows the delay.

storyboard.claim: Late praise has no emotional impact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock stands alone in the frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Object replaces the manager; the delay becomes the picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock is read as elapsed time.

explainedBy: The reward must link to the behavior it follows, so the praise has to come right after the act.

storyboard.claim: Praise links to the behavior only when it is immediate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from specific behavior to praise right away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clock replaced by a cause-effect flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause and effect of timely praise.

explainedBy: A narrated analogy: teaching a baby to walk shows how praise accelerates learning.
noVisual: No child in the cast; the analogy is narrated, not drawn.

storyboard.claim: The walking analogy shows how learning speeds up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout names the analogy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Flow replaced by a text-led analogy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the analogy so the viewer knows what it is.

explainedBy: We understand learning in personal life and forget it in corporate life; two buckets show the contrast.

storyboard.claim: We learn well in personal life and forget at work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two buckets: personal life and corporate life.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new diagram contrasts the two settings.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the contrast visible.

explainedBy: A learner stands up and falls right away; the first fall is the start of the story.

storyboard.claim: The learner falls immediately after standing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young man tips over, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the walking sequence with one person.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the fall as a physical act.

explainedBy: The learner is stood up again; the adult gets them back on their feet.

storyboard.claim: You stand them up again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man, now standing, neutral face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person; the fall becomes a recovery.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the repetition of standing.

explainedBy: The learner manages a wobbly half step, the first sign of progress.

storyboard.claim: The learner takes a small wobbling step.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man, face brightening.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person; expression changes from neutral to happy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The face marks the first progress.

explainedBy: Parents cheer and hug the child for the wobble; praising the wobble is the action.

storyboard.claim: The wobble is praised with cheering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man celebrating.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Action changes from idle to celebrate.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reinforcement as a deed.

explainedBy: The praise makes the learner want that feeling again, so they walk to repeat it.

storyboard.claim: The learner tries again to get the reward.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man walking, happy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Action changes to walk; the learner now repeats.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the repetition as motion.

explainedBy: Repeated tries rewire the brain until the wobble becomes a confident walk.

storyboard.claim: Repetition turns the wobble into a confident walk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man walking, same stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Only the callout changes, from the wobble to the confident walk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the result of the repetition.

explainedBy: The question asks where praising a wobble ends and enabling poor work begins.

storyboard.claim: The question: where does praise become enabling?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager speaks, neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Stage moves back to the office manager.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the question as spoken.

explainedBy: Praising a flawed report just because the person tried produces a department of flawed reports.

storyboard.claim: Praising a flawed report leads to more flawed reports.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul holds a report.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Paul replaces the manager as the one with the work.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the report, since a held note is easy to miss.

explainedBy: Praising the bare minimum makes the employee think they are a superstar while the work is terrible.

storyboard.claim: Praising the bare minimum is the mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager points at the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager returns with a pointing gesture.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the praise as rejected.

explainedBy: Managers default to being harsh critics out of fear of lowering the bar.

storyboard.claim: Harsh criticism is the default for managers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, angry face, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face changes to angry to show the harsh critic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry marks the harshness, not a threat.

explainedBy: You praise the wobble only when the employee is new; a flow shows when the praise applies.

storyboard.claim: Praise the wobble only for a new employee.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from new to the job to praise the wobble.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager replaced with a condition-action flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows when the praise applies.

explainedBy: The same rule holds for an experienced employee on an unfamiliar new project.

storyboard.claim: A new project also counts as the new stage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow kept.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same diagram; only the callout adds the second case.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the experienced-employee case.

explainedBy: The manager watches closely and catches the employee doing something right, even a small step.

storyboard.claim: The manager catches small right steps.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, happy, points at the young man.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Diagram gives way to the manager and the employee.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the catching as a deed.

explainedBy: The narrator rejects endless praise; the goalpost moves once the job is known.

storyboard.claim: Endless participation praise is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager speaks, neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager alone; the praise is rejected.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the phrase.

explainedBy: Once the employee is a high performer, the expectation is steady work, not a wobble.

storyboard.claim: A high performer walks steadily.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young man walks, happy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the young man, now walking.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the mastered walk.

explainedBy: Demanding perfection and punishing every stumble freezes the learner in place.

storyboard.claim: Punishing stumbles freezes the learner.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person; expression changes to afraid.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows fear as the result of punishment.

explainedBy: After punishment the learner never takes a risk again, withdrawn and blank.

storyboard.claim: The learner stops taking risks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same young man, blank face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person; expression changes to blank.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows withdrawal as apathy.

explainedBy: Praise done right is specific recognition of a step toward the shared goal, not flattery.

storyboard.claim: Specific praise aims at the shared goal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon with the manager, happy, pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A target now marks the goal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target reads as aiming at a goal.

explainedBy: People sprint in the wrong direction after a big mistake; the compass shows the direction is off.

storyboard.claim: Big mistakes come from sprinting the wrong way.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A compass icon alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager and employee replaced by the compass.
storyboard.addedInformation: The compass reads as direction.

explainedBy: The one-minute redirect is the third tool, used on a massive mistake.

storyboard.claim: The one-minute redirect handles a big mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager points, neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Compass replaced by the manager.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the tool being introduced.

explainedBy: The story now follows John Levy, an experienced engineer.

storyboard.claim: The story introduces John Levy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John, neutral, standing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New person on screen.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the character.

explainedBy: John made a big mistake that cost the company time or money.

storyboard.claim: John made a costly mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John slumps, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person; expression and action change.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the mistake through the face and slump.

explainedBy: The manager confronts John at once and checks the facts before anything else.

storyboard.claim: The manager confirms facts first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager holds a magnifier beside John.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager joins John; a magnifier appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier reads as checking facts.

explainedBy: The manager states exactly what John did: bypassed the QA protocol and caused a crash.

storyboard.claim: John bypassed the QA protocol.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage, magnifier still held.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Only the callout changes to the stated fact.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific error.

explainedBy: The manager expresses frustration and anger about the impact on reputation and the support team.

storyboard.claim: The mistake puts the reputation at risk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, angry, talking to John.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Magnifier dropped; face changes to angry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry marks the confrontation.

explainedBy: A painful, heavy, unblinking pause follows the strong words.

storyboard.claim: The manager holds a heavy pause.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same two people, quiet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face and action become still; the pause is the change.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pause as a deed.

explainedBy: The manager lets the dread sink in; John sits stewing, terrified.

storyboard.claim: John is terrified in the pause.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John slumps, afraid, the manager beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: John leads; his fear is the picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Afraid marks terror, not surprise.

explainedBy: John expects to be handed a box to pack his desk, the sign of being let go.

storyboard.claim: John expects to be let go.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage, John afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Only the callout names the expectation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The box is named as the sign.

explainedBy: The manager softens and tells John he is better than this mistake, the pivot.

storyboard.claim: The manager pivots to warmth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, happy, looks at John.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Manager leads again; face changes to happy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Happy is genuine warmth here.

explainedBy: The manager says John is one of his best engineers and that he trusts him.

storyboard.claim: The manager expresses trust in John.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, happy, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Action changes to talk; the callout adds the trust.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the trust.

explainedBy: The whole reversal from dread to trust is an emotional roller coaster built on behavioral psychology.

storyboard.claim: The reversal from dread to trust is an emotional roller coaster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage as before.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Only the callout changes to name the swing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the overall emotional swing.
